passage:
A mountain town became a dark-sky area. Streetlights were changed, advertising lights were limited, and hotels gave guests red flashlights for night walks.
Tourists came to see stars. Local businesses benefited, but some residents worried about safety. The town kept lights at crossings and emergency areas while reducing unnecessary brightness.
Students visiting the town saw more stars than they had ever seen before.
The dark sky was not created by adding something. It was protected by taking excess away.
Modern life often solves problems with more light, more screens, and more signs. The town showed that sometimes less allows people to see more.
